title: Set 71

sentences.ko: 남는 방 책상에 놓을 의자를 400달러 주고 주문했는데, 그게 도착한 바로 그 주에 회사에서 이제 주 3일 출근이라고 하더라고. 그래서 화요일이랑 금요일에 앉는 게 다야. 아내는 자꾸 그걸 왕좌라고 부르는데, 뭐 맞는 말이지. 게다가 짜증낼 데도 없어. 내 탓이잖아.
sentences.text: I ordered this chair for the desk in the spare room, four hundred dollars, and it showed up the same week they told us we're back in the office three days a week. So I sit in it Tuesday and Friday and that's about it. My wife keeps calling it the throne, which, yeah, fair. And I can't even be annoyed at anybody but myself.

alts.text: So I bought this chair for the desk in the spare room, four hundred bucks, and it turned up the same week they told us we're back in the office three days a week. So I'm in it Tuesday and Friday and that's about it. My wife keeps calling it the throne, which, yeah, fair. And the only person I can be mad at is me.

I purchased this chair for the desk in the spare room, four hundred dollars, and it arrived the same week we were informed that we are back in the office three days a week. So I sit in it on Tuesday and Friday, and that is about all. My wife keeps calling it the throne, which, admittedly, is fair. And I cannot be annoyed with anyone but myself.

sentences.note: **that's about it** 은 그게 전부라는 뜻으로, 앞에 말한 것 말고는 더 없다고 마무리할 때 씁니다. **which, yeah, fair** 는 상대의 놀림이 맞는 말이라고 순순히 인정하는 말투입니다.

sentences.ko: 우린 넓게 살고 싶어서 여기로 나왔고, 넓긴 넓어. 근데 이제 뭘 하든 차를 몰아야 해. 진짜 뭘 하든. 우유 한 통 사러 가는 데 왕복 20분이야. 그래서 다시 시내 쪽 집을 보고 있는데, 더 좁은데 더 비싸. 따져 보면 손해인 거 나도 알아. 근데 봄 이후로 친구들을 한 번도 못 봤어. 그게 제일 힘들어.
sentences.text: We moved out here for the space, and we got the space, but now I drive for everything, and I mean everything, a gallon of milk is a twenty minute round trip. So I've been looking at places back in town, and they're smaller and they cost more, which I know is a bad trade on paper. But I haven't seen my friends since the spring, and that's the part that's getting to me.

alts.text: The whole point of moving out here was the space, and sure, we got the space, but now I drive for everything, and I mean everything, a gallon of milk is a twenty minute round trip. So I've been looking at places back in town, and they're smaller and they cost more, which I know is a bad trade on paper. But I haven't seen my friends since the spring, and that's the thing that's really getting to me.

We moved out here for the space, and we did get the space, but now I drive for everything, and I do mean everything; a gallon of milk is a twenty minute round trip. So I have been looking at places back in town, and they are smaller and they cost more, which I know is a poor trade on paper. But I have not seen my friends since the spring, and that is the part that is getting to me.

sentences.note: **a bad trade on paper** 는 숫자만 놓고 보면 손해라는 뜻으로, 그걸 알면서도 마음이 그쪽으로 기울 때 씁니다. **that's getting to me** 는 그게 마음에 걸려서 힘들다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 웃지 마. 나 오늘 한 층 올라가는데 엘리베이터 타. 제니가 일요일에 그 스피닝 수업 가자고 꼬드겼거든. 나 어릴 때 이후로 자전거를 타 본 적이 없는데, 당연히 거기 있는 사람들만큼 세게 했지. 진짜 아픈 건 계단 내려갈 때야. 그리고 3일째가 2일째보다 더 아프대.
sentences.text: Don't laugh, but I'm taking the elevator up one floor today. Jenny talked me into that spin class on Sunday, and I haven't been on a bike since I was a kid, so of course I went as hard as everybody else in there. Going down the stairs is the part that actually hurts, and apparently day three is worse than day two.

alts.text: Okay, don't laugh, but I'm riding the elevator up one floor today. Jenny roped me into that spin class on Sunday, and I haven't been on a bike since I was a kid, so obviously I went just as hard as everyone else in there. Going down the stairs is the part that actually hurts, and apparently day three is worse than day two.

Please do not laugh, but I am taking the elevator up one floor today. Jenny persuaded me to attend that spin class on Sunday, and I have not been on a bicycle since I was a child, so naturally I worked as hard as everyone else in the room. Going down the stairs is the part that actually hurts, and apparently day three is worse than day two.

sentences.note: **talked me into** 는 설득해서 하게 만들었다는 뜻으로, 원래는 별로 안 내켰다는 뉘앙스가 들어 있습니다. **so of course** 는 뻔한 결과를 스스로 놀리듯 말할 때 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 이거 고르는 데만 20분째야. 벌써 10시 다 됐어. 봐, 네가 고를 거면 끝까지 안 자고 봐야지. 토요일에도 시작하기도 전에 잠들었잖아. 그래서 일요일에 그 첫 부분 너랑 처음부터 다시 봤고. 그러니까 그 요리 나오는 거 틀든가, 아니면 내가 고르고 넌 불평하기 없기.
sentences.text: We've been at this for twenty minutes and it's almost ten already. Look, if you're picking, you have to actually stay awake for it, because on Saturday you were out before it even got going, and then I sat through that whole opening again with you on Sunday. So either put on the cooking one, or I pick and you don't get to complain about it.

alts.text: Twenty minutes we've been doing this and it's almost ten already. Look, if you're picking, you've gotta actually stay awake for it, cause Saturday you were out before it even got going, and then I sat through that whole opening again with you on Sunday. So either put on the cooking one, or I pick and you don't get to complain about it.

We have been at this for twenty minutes and it is almost ten already. If you are going to choose, you do have to stay awake for it, because on Saturday you were asleep before it even got going, and then I sat through that entire opening again with you on Sunday. So either put on the cooking one, or I will choose and you may not complain about it.

sentences.note: **you were out** 은 잠들었다는 뜻입니다. **you don't get to complain** 은 그럴 자격이 없다는 말로, 조건을 걸 때 쓰는 표현입니다.

sentences.ko: 주문한 게 지난주 수요일부터 같은 창고에 계속 있어. 배송 조회도 하나도 안 바뀌고. 아무도 손을 안 대고 있는 것 같아. 근데 그게 여행 갈 때 쓸 캐리어라서, 오늘 안에 그냥 하나 사러 나갈지 정해야 돼. 토요일 아침에 출발하거든. 채팅 상담은 계속 업데이트를 기다리라고만 하고, 사람이랑 통화할 수 있는 번호도 없어.
sentences.text: My order has been sitting at the same warehouse since last Wednesday and the tracking hasn't moved at all, so I don't think anybody actually has their hands on it. And it's the suitcase for the trip, so I have to decide today whether I just go out and buy one, because we leave Saturday morning. The chat thing keeps telling me to wait for an update, and there's no number you can call to get an actual person.

alts.text: My order's been stuck at the same warehouse since last Wednesday and the tracking hasn't budged at all, so I don't think anybody's actually got their hands on it. And it's the suitcase for the trip, so I've gotta decide today whether I just go out and buy one, cause we leave Saturday morning. The chat thing keeps telling me to wait for an update, and there's no number you can call to get an actual person.

My order has been sitting at the same warehouse since last Wednesday and the tracking has not moved at all, so I do not believe anyone actually has their hands on it. And it is the suitcase for the trip, so I have to decide today whether I simply go out and buy one, because we leave Saturday morning. The chat service keeps telling me to wait for an update, and there is no number one can call to reach an actual person.

sentences.note: **has their hands on it** 은 누군가 그 물건을 실제로 손에 쥐고 처리하고 있다는 뜻입니다. **the tracking hasn't moved** 는 배송 조회 상태가 그대로라는 말입니다.

reviewed: 1번 casual: "it turns up the same week they tell us" 처럼 현재형이 섞여 있어 앞뒤 시제가 어긋났습니다. 지난 일을 말하는 것이므로 "turned up ... they told us" 로 맞췄습니다.
1번 casual: "there's nobody I can even be mad at except me" 가 입에 잘 안 붙어서 "the only person I can be mad at is me" 로 바꿨습니다. 뜻은 그대로입니다.
2번 casual: "that's the bit that's getting to me" 의 the bit 은 영국식이라 미국 말투(gallon, elevator)와 어긋납니다. "that's the thing that's really getting to me" 로 바꿨습니다.
2번 note: "그래도 하겠다는 말이 뒤에 옵니다" 라고 했는데 문장 뒤에 오는 것은 그게 아니라 이사하고 싶은 이유입니다. 문장에 맞게 설명을 고쳤습니다.
3번 casual: "No laughing, but" 은 원어민이 잘 쓰지 않는 말입니다. "Okay, don't laugh, but" 으로 바꿨습니다.
3번 casual: "got me into that spin class" 는 그 수업에 입문시켰다는 뜻으로 읽혀 원래 뜻(꼬드겨서 데려갔다)과 어긋납니다. "roped me into" 로 바꿨습니다.
5번 note: 별표로 감싼 **nobody actually has their hands on it** 이 문장에 그대로 나오지 않습니다(문장은 anybody). 실제로 나오는 표현으로 고쳤습니다.
